chapter_summary: Dawn approaches before anyone has seen what she made. Debolina asks whether work without witnesses can still address the world.

spatality.place: the scaffold at the hour when the sky begins to grey behind the haveli
spatality.route: from the wall to the lane to the sky, and back to the wall
spatality.texture: cold metal of the lamp, dew on the rope, the first bird absurdly loud

poetic_parameters.movement: Language Poetry — fragmented field, here the hour before witnesses exist.
writing_skills: fragments of ordinary sound breaking the meditation
a question repeated with shifting emphasis
close on a factual observation that withholds judgement
poetic_parameters.image_seed: the lamp still lit while the sky behind the wall has already turned blue-grey
poetic_parameters.volta: from fearing the unwitnessed hour to doubting whether witness changes the work at all
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: the long open a of dawn held against the clipped k of clock, dark, back
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: sentences that begin confidently and trail into fragments as the light arrives
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Chapter twelve counted the past; this poem faces the future of a single morning and refuses to answer whether it will be seen.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: grey light, unread pages, a door opening onto nobody
poetic_parameters.address: the coming day, spoken to as a creditor
poetic_parameters.closing_move: a flat statement of fact that lands harder than any question
